title: PARS/dsRNA-Seq
scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic: PolyA RNA enters separate S1 and V1 nuclease routes, each followed by random fragmentation and reverse transcription to cDNA. The catalogue supplies the downstream sequencing/comparison interface. PARS/PARS-Seq naming and the two-treatment comparison are supported; a distinct dsRNA-Seq implementation is not resolved by the supplied evidence. This records the family-level depiction, not every PARS implementation or a laboratory recipe.

states.label: Comparative RNA secondary-structure evidence
features: Comparison of single-strand-sensitive and double-strand-sensitive digestion patterns provides evidence about paired versus unpaired RNA regions.

operations.label: RNase digestion — RNase S1
operations.description: A parallel portion of the depicted PolyA RNA is treated with RNase S1. The structured RNA is converted into shorter RNA fragments carrying the depicted 5′ P/3′ OH ends. Icons occupy the exposed loop in the upper row, supporting preferential cleavage of single-stranded regions. The icons identify the enzyme acting on RNA, not a retained library component. The two rows are parallel treatments, not sequential nuclease digestions.
operations.mechanism: Structure-sensitive nuclease digestion as depicted for RNase S1; the catalogue cautions that enzyme digestion can be nonspecific.
operations.information_effect: RNA cleavage produces a treatment-associated pattern of fragments/endpoints related to accessibility of single-stranded regions. Preference is evidence about structure, not proof of perfectly specific cleavage.

method_scopes.rationale: PARS expands to parallel analysis of RNA structure in the diagram and primary abstract; the catalogue uses PARS-Seq and the inspected review explicitly uses PARS-Seq for comparing single- and double-strand-specific nuclease libraries. This supports the two-treatment interpretation of this schematic. The diagram supplies the end groups, random-fragmentation order and cDNA stages; the primary abstract does not independently verify those reaction details. Sequencing and comparison are text-supported extensions, not additional drawn panels.
